Research & VisionSupporting continuity in diabetes care

A multilingual, privacy-respecting approach to helping patients stay connected between clinic visits.

Research & Vision

What problem are we solving?

Diabetes care is a lifelong process, yet continuity between appointments can be difficult to sustain.

Diabetes care is a lifelong process, yet many patients experience it as a sequence of isolated clinic visits. Between consultations, regular monitoring, scheduled follow-ups, nutrition counselling, lifestyle changes, and patient education often lose momentum. Patients may disengage because of work constraints, financial pressure, digital barriers, caregiver dependence, stigma, or diabetes-related fatigue.

For diabetologists and care teams, fragmented records and manual calls/messages make it difficult to identify unmet follow-up needs, respond to patient-reported concerns, coordinate dietician support, and deliver timely, personalised encouragement at scale. We envision an assistive, privacy-respecting, multilingual solution that keeps patients engaged between visits without replacing clinical judgement.

The Sugar Coat Concept

Five pillars of connected diabetes support

Designed to make clinician-approved care plans easier to follow in daily life.

AI Care Companion

A voice-first, supportive guide—not a second doctor. It understands each patient’s routine, explains clinician- and dietician-approved guidance in simple language, and provides timely, caring reminders.

Care Connections

With patient consent, it helps complete practical next steps: booking visits, requesting lab reports, reaching pharmacies or dieticians, and involving a caregiver.

Care Passport

A secure, patient-owned hub for health records, including reports, prescriptions, care plans, appointments, and consented routine updates.

Clinic Intelligence Layer

A clear, non-clinical view of each patient’s latest updates, pending actions, requests, and reported barriers for the care team.

Community & Education

Curated, trustworthy patient education, local health camps, and structured milestones to sustain long-term motivation.

Sugar Coat is an assistive coordination and engagement concept. It does not provide medical diagnosis, treatment advice, or automated clinical decision-making.
